newsitem.title: UK: BOF's Trichet says stability pact progressing.
newsitem.headline: BOF's Trichet says stability pact progressing.

text.p: Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet said on Wednesday that discussions on the fiscal stability pact under European Monetary Union are progressing, though some matters still need to be settled.

"Discussions on the fiscal stability pact are progressing, even though some matters remain to be settled," Trichet said. One example of an issue to be settled was the definition of "exceptional cicrcumstances" under which the Maastricht three percent fiscal deficit target might be exceeded, he said.
In a speech to the Confederation of British Industry Trichet said that France currently meets four out of the five Maastricht convergence criteria.

"As for the...criterion that sets the maximum ratio of general government deficit to GDP at three percent, the situation is improving gradually," he said. "Our deficit stands probably at around four percent of GDP this year."
Trichet said French efforts at short and medium term fiscal adjustment will be pursued.
Trichet said confidence in the Euro single currency must be established.
"An adequate policy mix will ensure the credibility of the Euro as a solid and stable international currency," he said.
"I would like to stress that confidence in the Euro must be established at a very high level right now and not only after January 1, 1999."
Trichet said this was because 10-year rates are already incorporating two years of French Franc and almost eight years of Euro.
Trichet also said: "Stronger growth is clearly under way in Europe and in France."
He added: "This ongoing stronger growth is very healthy, with low inflation, a significant current account surplus and a low level of indebtedness in the private sector and within households."
Trichet's comments were contained in a speech prepared for delivery to the CBI dinner. A copy was released to the media.
